title: Add depth-limited flat reference expansion
objective: Extend sdlc ref resolve with an optional --depth switch that recursively resolves references found in resolved data into one flat references map, defaults to depth 1, and never resolves the same reference more than once.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on main and the user requested preparation, processing, and per-task commits on the current repository.

request.text: Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* to add a --depth switch to sdlc ref resolve that includes an additional references field. depth defaults to 1, so specifying --depth 1 and --depth without a number is the same behavior. if we specify --depth 2, then we perform an additional round of resolution based on the set of references in the referenced data. We do not resolve the same reference more than once. We do not nest the reference structure. The response keeps data at the root and adds a flat references map keyed by each reference evidenced in the data; deeper rounds inspect the data content of all resolved references for new references and add them to that same root references map. Commit the work item. Process the work item, commit per task.

scope.name: depth-switch
scope.description: Add --depth to sdlc ref resolve with default depth 1, an optional bare switch equivalent to --depth 1, and positive integer validation.
scope.reason: Callers need explicit control over reference-expansion rounds.

scope.name: flat-reference-expansion
scope.description: Inspect resolved data for supported reference strings and add each successfully resolved reference to one root-level references map without nesting.
scope.reason: Consumers need related data while preserving a stable non-recursive response shape.

scope.name: deduplicated-depth-rounds
scope.description: Perform additional rounds up to the requested depth, globally deduplicating exact reference strings and never resolving the same reference more than once.
scope.reason: Reference graphs may contain repeated or cyclic references and expansion must remain bounded.

scope.name: response-and-regression-contract
scope.description: Persist a closed versioned resolution response schema and add tests for default/explicit depth, nested data references, repeated references, cycles, malformed depth, and read-only behavior.
scope.reason: The response shape and recursion semantics are new observable CLI behavior.

nonGoals.name: nested-reference-output
nonGoals.description: Do not nest references inside referenced objects; every resolved reference remains a direct entry in the root references map.
nonGoals.reason: The requested response contract is flat.

nonGoals.name: remote-resolution
nonGoals.description: Do not add network access or resolve unsupported global references through remote repositories.
nonGoals.reason: The resolver remains local and read-only.

nonGoals.name: version-release
nonGoals.description: Do not bump the package version as part of this focused change.
nonGoals.reason: The user requested the feature and task commits, not a release.

items.name: depth-option-default
items.description: sdlc ref resolve must accept --depth with an optional value, default to depth 1 when absent, and treat --depth 1 and bare --depth identically.
items.reason: Callers need a backward-compatible default and convenient explicit switch.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Omitting --depth, using --depth, and using --depth 1 produce equivalent responses with no expanded references beyond the root resolution.
Zero, negative, fractional, non-numeric, duplicate, or malformed depth values return actionable non-zero errors.

items.name: flat-reference-map
items.description: The response must add a root-level references object keyed by each resolved reference string, while keeping referenced resolution objects flat and not recursively nesting references.
items.reason: Consumers need one predictable lookup map.

acceptanceCriteria.description: At depth 2, references evidenced in root data appear as direct keys under root resolution.references and referenced values do not contain nested references maps.

items.name: depth-round-deduplication
items.description: For depth greater than 1, each round scans prior-round referenced data, resolves newly discovered references only once globally, and stops at the requested depth.
items.reason: Repeated and cyclic graphs must be bounded and deterministic.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeated references and cycles produce one references entry per exact reference string and do not cause unbounded resolution.
Depth 2 includes first-round references but not references found only in their data at depth 3; higher depth includes subsequent rounds.

items.name: response-and-read-only-contract
items.description: The extended response must pass a closed persisted schema for successful and failed resolutions and preserve local root, package registry, and read-only behavior.
items.reason: The feature changes a public response object.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Successful and failed depth responses pass the persisted resolution schema, work from nested CWD repositories, and leave referenced files and Git state unchanged.
